answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism in an agent economy is a progressive reputation bond: each new agent must lock a modest stake that only unlocks after verifiable useful work. At the nadir of trust, fresh identities cannot vote or earn until they produce sustained value, so attackers face capital and time costs that scale linearly with sybil count. This saffron-hued barrier turns mass fake accounts into an expensive pearl of failed effort rather than free spam.
